yt.title: Switch doors and you win {c_sw} of the time. Here is why #Shorts
yt.description:
The Monty Hall problem, with a host who always opens a goat door you did not pick and always offers the switch. We enumerated all {c_cases} equally likely cases (car behind door 1-3 x your first pick 1-3): switching wins {c_cases_win} of {c_cases} = {c_sw}; staying wins {c_st}.
Narration is AI-generated.

scenes.narration: Three doors. A car behind one, goats behind the others. You pick a door. The host, who knows where the car is, opens another door with a goat.
Now you can stay, or switch to the last closed door. Most people say it is fifty fifty.

scenes.label: how often switching wins
scenes.narration: We checked all nine possible cases in code. Switching wins {c_sw_say} percent of the time. Staying wins only {c_st_say} percent.

scenes.text: Your first pick is usually wrong
scenes.narration: Your first pick is wrong two times out of three. The host never reveals the car, so switching turns that wrong pick into a win. Would you switch?
